questions.q: What changes when resilience becomes a moral expectation?
choices: Setbacks are accepted as unavoidable limits.
Perseverance is rewarded only after success.
Circumstances may be ignored when endurance is demanded.
Students gain more freedom to reconsider their goals.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: What separates agency from endurance in the second paragraph?
choices: Whether renewed effort has a realistic chance to help.
Whether the pupil receives praise from others.
Whether improvement can be measured in a short test.
Whether the pupil remains visibly determined.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Why can celebrating endurance be convenient for an institution?
choices: It makes pupils less interested in their grades.
It proves the institution provides enough support.
It shows that all barriers are personal choices.
It avoids questioning why the obstacles persist.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: What is the effect of saying that indicators 'colonise' what they should illuminate?
choices: It suggests that indicators are always inaccurate.
It portrays measurement as taking over educational values.
It praises increasingly detailed progress reports.
It claims that only measurable activities are useful.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Why is the learner who explores an unfamiliar idea contrasted with one drilling familiar questions?
choices: To show that exploration must always produce better marks.
To claim that practice questions are educationally useless.
To expose what a narrow progress metric can overlook.
To demonstrate that difficult ideas should be avoided.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: How does the final paragraph avoid simply rejecting resilience?
choices: It keeps perseverance valuable but makes it conditional and discerning.
It argues that individual responsibility should be removed.
It recommends abandoning all performance indicators.
It presents rest as a substitute for learning.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: What limitation is implied by inspirational stories told only after a struggle has ended?
choices: They are useful only to high-achieving pupils.
They prove that continued effort is always rewarded.
They make it impossible to learn from the past.
They may conceal how uncertain persistence felt at the time.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Why might choosing to abandon a goal indicate maturity?
choices: It guarantees that the next goal will be easier.
It can reflect judgement about whether persistence remains worthwhile.
It means the student is no longer accountable.
It shows that measurable success is undesirable.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: A school records only how quickly students improve test scores. Which policy best follows the essay?
choices: Reward the fastest learners without further evidence.
Remove all assessment from every course.
Consider exploration, support and the limits of the measure.
Use the same indicator for hobbies and leisure activities.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Which educational culture most closely matches the writer's ideal?
choices: One that gives pupils support and freedom to reassess aims.
One that requires pupils to persist in every chosen task.
One that treats rest as proof of low ambition.
One that replaces judgement with more frequent measurements.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.
